title: Control: the elevated key player, alarms and recordings
tagline: The one admin process that presses keys, its Lie Detector guard, and the recorders
summary: MapleStory runs as administrator, so one small elevated process, the key player, presses every key and click; everything else hands it JSON plans through files in `gamelab/lab`. Around it sit the Lie Detector safety net (a watchdog 4 times a second, the alarm file, PC paging, phone pushes, a per-cycle recording), the rolling 5-minute recording that saves what led up to an alarm, the perception service's live helpers for the Lie Detector's mini-games, and the Alt+Enter fix for a game window of the wrong size.
details_md:
### Why one elevated process
Windows blocks input sent by normal programs into an administrator window, and the game runs as administrator. So `python -m gamelab player --elevate` starts one process through a UAC prompt (ShellExecute "runas"), and the hunt, the perception service and every command stay unelevated. They talk through files: a plan is `lab/inbox/<id>.json`, claimed as `.running`, cut short by `.cancel`, taken over by `.splice`; its result is `lab/outbox/<id>.json`. The player's rules: it runs no code from plans (they are data that `validate` checks), presses keys only with the game in front (checked before every key), moves the pointer only inside the game, loads its code and keys once (only `lab/alarm_keys.json` is read again, and it can only move which keys her moves and pet food are on), stops itself (`lab/STOP`, 24 idle hours, or after a Lie Detector), and lets go of every held key when a plan is cancelled or ends.

### The Lie Detector
The game's anti-bot check comes in several forms: a countdown window (the Violetta shuffle game), the mouse mini-game and its notice 10 s ahead, an image quiz and its warning 30 s ahead, and the Truth Booth a failed test sends her to. The player's `Watchdog` looks at the game 4 times a second, idle or not. On a sighting:

1. the `Alarm` event is set first: the key thread's waits end and a running plan stops within about 10 ms, its held keys let go;
2. `lab/ALARM.json` and a screenshot are written and the PC is paged (control.alarm), the phone pushed (control.notify);
3. the cycle is recorded look by look (control.lie_recorder), and the rolling recorder saves the 5 minutes before it and a lossless clip (control.rolling);
4. every plan is refused but four kinds (`alarm.PLAN_KINDS`): a pet-food tap (3 a minute), her retreat's moves for 12 s (the running hunt's behavior.retreat), and two kinds of strictly shaped mouse plan that the perception service's helpers send: the mini-game cursor (control.lie_tracking) and the Violetta answer and pass-dialog OK clicks (control.violetta_live);
5. every other gamelab command refuses to send keys while the alarm file exists (exit code 3).

An answered Lie Detector (off the screen 10 s, no Truth Booth seen) clears its own alarm and plans resume. A cycle that saw the Truth Booth keeps the player locked: a person runs `clear-alarm`, the player stops 10 s after the screen is clear, and only a person's UAC click starts it again.

### The recordings
| What | Who | Where |
|---|---|---|
| per-look scores of each cycle | the player's Watchdog (lie_recorder) | `lab/lie_detector/<stamp>/` |
| the last 5 minutes, lossless, in memory | the perception service (recording + rolling, 15 frames a second), or `gamelab recorder` (its own grabs, 10 a second) | memory; saves below |
| 5 minutes before an alarm | rolling | `<cycle folder>/before/` |
| the alarm's clip, lossless: 2 s before the first frame showing it to 5 s after the test's last sight (3 minutes after the alarm at most) | rolling | `lab/alarm_clips/` |
| the 5 minutes before a Truth Booth no test was seen before (cause unknown), at once | rolling | `lab/booth_unknown/` |
| on demand (`save-recent`) | rolling | `lab/recent/` |

Saves made in the perception service are encoded by a separate partwriter process, so they don't share Python's lock with the frame loop.

### Window sizing
The eyes are built for a 1366x768 client. When it's another size or the game draws off its client, control.window_size sends Alt+Enter twice through the player (full screen and back), checking before every press that the alarm isn't up, no Lie Detector is on the picture, no plan is running and no other process is trying, at most 4 tries an hour.

### Processes in this slice
The elevated player (watchdog thread inside); the perception service, which hosts the recording, the mini-game tracker and the Violetta solver; their child processes (the partwriter per save, the target tracker during an alarm); and, where the service doesn't record, the standalone `gamelab recorder`.

modules.title: The key player
modules.tagline: The one elevated process that plays JSON key plans, watched over by a Lie Detector watchdog
modules.summary: `python -m gamelab player --elevate` runs `serve`: a single administrator process (one UAC click) that takes plans from `lab/inbox` in name order, presses their keys, mouse moves and clicks on time on a thread of its own, optionally records the game's client area, and answers in `lab/outbox`. A `Watchdog` thread looks at the game 4 times a second for the Lie Detector; on a sighting it sets the `Alarm` event (keys stop within about 10 ms), raises the alarm, pages, pushes the phone and records the cycle, and from then on `alarm_refusal` lets only four kinds of plan through.
modules.details_md:
MapleStory runs as administrator, and Windows blocks input from normal programs into an administrator window. So every key gamelab sends goes through this one elevated process, and everything else runs unelevated and talks to it through files. The safety rules are what make it acceptable to run elevated:

| Rule | How the code enforces it |
|---|---|
| No code from plans | plans are JSON data; `validate` checks every event, time and option |
| Game in front only | checked before a plan and again before every single key (`win32.foreground_title`) |
| Pointer only inside the game | mouse moves are client pixels; one outside the client area is skipped |
| Fixed at start | code, config.toml and the key list are read once (only `lab/alarm_keys.json` is re-read: it can move her move and pet-food keys, nothing more); the watchdog's perception imports are made only when it is created |
| Stops itself | `lab/STOP`, 24 idle hours (`IDLE_LIMIT_S`), or after a Lie Detector once a person cleared it |
| Cancel files | `lab/inbox/<id>.cancel` is checked between 15 ms wait steps; every held key is let go |
| Lie Detector watchdog | 4 looks a second; the alarm event stops keys mid-plan |

### A plan's life
1. control.client writes `lab/inbox/<id>.json` atomically.
2. `_serve` polls every 10 ms, takes the first by name and claims it by renaming it `<id>.running` (from then on the client can cancel it but not withdraw it). `_read_plan` retries every 5 ms for up to `READ_RETRY_S` (0.5 s) while Windows refuses the file.
3. `Player.run` checks and plays it; `_answer` writes the result to `lab/outbox/<id>.json` via a `.tmp` file and an atomic replace. Output names come from the sanitized file name, never from the plan's contents.

### Timing
The key thread waits for each event's time in 15 ms steps (`WAIT_STEP_S`) slept on the halt event, so a Lie Detector sighting ends the wait at once, and waits the last 20 ms (`FINAL_S`) with `_sleep_until`: `time.sleep` steps of at most 10 ms that wake 2 ms early, spinning only the final 4 ms. Waiting with `_sleep_until` all the way had cost 0.12 cores while plans ran back to back; the stepped wait costs about 0.02. The serve loop runs inside `win32.precise_timers()` (a 1 ms system timer).

### Splices
A plan can be taken over mid-flight: `<running id>.splice` (written by `control.client.splice`) is claimed, validated, never a resize or recording, held to the alarm rules like any plan, and at its `at_ms` the keys not in its `held` list are let go and the missing ones pressed; the old plan is answered with the problem `spliced` (`{to, at_ms, late_ms}`). The player advertises this in `lab/player.json` (`SPLICE` = 1) so the navigator knows it can splice instead of cutting and resending.

### The Lie Detector
See `Watchdog.tick` and `alarm_refusal`. In short: the alarm event is set first, then the alarm file, screenshot and paging (control.alarm), the phone push (control.notify) and the cycle's recording (control.lie_recorder). An answered Lie Detector (off the screen 10 s, no Truth Booth) clears its own alarm (`AUTO_RESUME`); a Truth Booth cycle keeps the player locked until `clear-alarm`, after which it stops and needs a person's UAC click to start again.

key_items.name: serve
key_items.summary: The player's entry point: refuses to start with the alarm up, cleans stale inbox files, builds the Player, the phone Pusher and the Watchdog, then runs `_serve` until it stops.
key_items.details_md: Steps: make `lab`, `lab/inbox`, `lab/outbox`; rotate `player.log` past 5 MB (`_rotate_log`); delete `lab/STOP`; return at once if `lab/ALARM.json` exists ("refusing to start: a Lie Detector alarm hasn't been cleared"); delete leftover `*.json`, `*.cancel`, `*.running`, `*.splice`, `*.spliced`; load config.toml once; build the unsafe-key list for the alarm's key file (`ALARM_UNSAFE` plus maplehelper's `[hotkeys]` and `[control]` keys); make `Player(allowed_keys(cfg.keys), title, alarm, keys=cfg.keys, keys_file=ALARM_KEYS)`; enable DPI awareness; `notify.Pusher.from_lab`; start the `Watchdog`; log what is allowed; write `lab/player.json` (`{"splice": 1, "pid", "started"}`), removed again when it stops.

key_items.name: Player.run
key_items.summary: Checks one plan and plays it: key events on a `key-player` thread, frames captured on the calling thread, every held key let go at the end.
key_items.details_md:
1. With the alarm event set and a kind not in `PLAN_KINDS`: the Lie Detector error at once. A plan of one of those kinds with only the alarm *file* up (raised by `watch --lie-detector`, not this player) is treated as if this player had seen it (`filed`), its retreat window counted from the file's `at`.
2. `validate`; `lie_cursor` and `lie_ok` plans always held to their exact shapes (`lie_cursor_refusal`, `lie_ok_refusal`); with the alarm up, `_with_alarm` -> `alarm_refusal`. A retreat gets a cutoff at `RETREAT_WINDOW_S` (12 s) after the sighting.
3. `window_client` resizes the client first (0.5 s to lay out); `focus` brings the game to the front (0.5 s) but never with the alarm up; then the game must be in front.
4. `t0` = now + `lead_ms` (default 100). A `key-player` thread runs `press_keys`: for each event `wait(due)` (cancel files, retreat cutoff, pending splice, halt event), the foreground checked again, then `_press` (win32 SendInput) or `window.move_cursor` (a generated trail, recorded as `trail`). A `lie_cursor`/`lie_ok` button press goes down only if the game is the window under the pointer (`window.pointer_on`).
5. Meanwhile, if the plan asked, mss grabs the region at `fps` for `duration_ms` (+ lead), every `scale`-th pixel, RGB; saved to `lab/outbox/<id>.npz` with each frame's time.
6. `finally`: every held key let go, the plan's `.cancel` and late `.splice` removed, a splice taken but never reached answered as cancelled.

The halt event is the player's `Alarm` for a normal plan; a plan let through with the alarm up gets a private `threading.Event`, so the alarm that is already up doesn't stop it.

key_items.name: Watchdog
key_items.summary: The `lie-detector-watch` daemon thread: one look at the game every 0.25 s, idle or not, and the Lie Detector's whole cycle from first sight to its end.
key_items.details_md: Made with `Watchdog(game_title, alarm, spotter=None, grab=None, interval=0.25, on_alarm=None, folder=None, log=None, end_s=None, cap_s=None, pusher=None, auto_resume=None, test_tail_s=None)`; it imports `perception.framecheck`, `perception.lie_detector`, `control.lie_recorder` and `control.alarm.raise_alarm` only here, so the elevated process loads them only when it watches. `run` sets OpenCV to one thread (its 24 threads cost 0.27 cores more at 4 looks a second), opens an mss grabber and schedules a look every `interval` from the *start* of the previous one (`due = max(due + interval, now)`): 4 looks a second, where waiting 0.25 s after each look (plus the look's own ~70 ms) had made 3.10 a second. A look that ran long (the paging's beeps) is followed at once, not caught up. `looked` is set after the first look: the player takes no plan before it, so a Lie Detector already on screen at start is seen before any key. Nothing that goes wrong in a look, the recording or the log stops it (`_trouble` logs the first failure of a kind and every 1000th). Its events: `looked`, `cleared` (a person cleared the alarm and the screen has been clear `end_s`: the player stops), `stopped`.

key_items.name: Watchdog.tick
key_items.signature: def tick(self, now: float, sct=None) -> None
key_items.summary: One look and everything that follows from it: first sight, re-raising, recording, phone pushes, the cycle's end and the alarm's clearing.
key_items.details_md:
1. `_look` -> a frame (RGB), a frame flagged "covered", or no frame and why ("no window", "minimized").
2. `_scores` -> each form's match / threshold; `seen` if any is >= 1; `tested` if a form other than the Truth Booth is.
3. A look without a frame resets `gone_since` (the Lie Detector may be up behind a minimized game); a covered frame with nothing seen counts towards gone (since 2026-10-29).
4. First sight with no cycle in progress: `alarm.set()` before anything else (keys stop within about 10 ms); `form` = the best-scoring form; `cause` = `UNKNOWN_CAUSE` for a Truth Booth with no test seen and outside a known stay; `_raise` (alarm file, screenshot, paging); then the recording starts with this first frame.
5. Seen again after someone deleted the alarm file mid-cycle: raised again and paged (`_raise_again`), so gamelab's commands keep refusing.
6. A look that sees a form: `pusher.seen` (the phone) and, if the Truth Booth is among the forms, its on-screen clock read (`_booth_seen`: the stay's end, the median of the readings). Every look while a recording runs: `recording.add`. The recording ends at `cap_s` (600 s), or `test_tail_s` (5 s) after the test's last sight; the cycle then goes on unrecorded, its folder's `cycle.live` touched (`lie_recorder.cycle_going`).
7. Gone for `end_s` (10 s): the cycle ends, `pusher.ended`; answered (no Truth Booth) with `auto_resume` -> `_resume`.
8. With the alarm set: once the file has been seen and is then gone with no cycle and the screen clear for `end_s`, `cleared` is set and the player stops.

key_items.name: alarm_refusal
key_items.signature: def alarm_refusal(plan: dict, keys: GameKeys | None, since: float | None, fed: list[float], now: float) -> str | None
key_items.summary: Why a plan can't run with the Lie Detector alarm up (None: it can). Only the four kinds in `alarm.PLAN_KINDS` go, each only in its exact form.
key_items.details_md:
- Any kind outside `PLAN_KINDS`, any window resize or recording: refused.
- `lie_cursor` -> `lie_cursor_refusal`; `lie_ok` -> `lie_ok_refusal` (clicks, see those).
- Otherwise no mouse at all, and the plan must start within `TAP_MAX_MS` (200 ms) of being taken (its `lead_ms`), so a plan let through can't hold the player.
- `pet_food`: exactly her pet-food key down then up, the up and any `end_ms` within 200 ms; at most `PET_FOOD_PER_MIN` (3) in any 60 s (`fed`).
- `retreat`: only her left, right, jump, up and down keys, every key pressed also released, and only while `since` <= `RETREAT_WINDOW_S` (12 s) after the sighting; refused if when it was seen isn't known.

`keys` is `Player.allowance()`: config.toml's keys, or the followed ones from `lab/alarm_keys.json` (control.alarm.AlarmKeys).

key_items.name: validate
key_items.signature: def validate(plan: dict, allowed: dict[str, Key]) -> None
key_items.summary: Raises ValueError unless a plan is well-formed data that only uses allowed keys.
key_items.details_md: Events are `[ms, key, "down"|"up"]` (a key in `allowed` or `lbutton`/`rbutton`) or `[ms, "mouse", x, y]` (non-negative client px); at most `MAX_EVENTS` (400), times sorted and within `MAX_PLAN_MS` (20 s). `end_ms` after the last event and within 20 s. `window_client` one of `window.CLIENT_SIZES` (1366x768, 1920x1080). `capture`: fps 0-60, duration 0-20 s, at most `MAX_FRAMES` (900) frames including the lead, scale 1-4, crop `[x, y, w, h]` of non-negative ints.

key_items.name: lie_cursor_refusal
key_items.summary: The two allowed shapes of a `lie_cursor` plan: one immediate mouse move inside the mini-game's board, or one Violetta answer click. Enforced whether or not the alarm is up.
key_items.details_md: Any mouse-button event selects the click form (`lie_answer_refusal`, which may not fall back to the board-wide move allowance). Otherwise: no resize or recording, no focus, `lead_ms` 0, no final wait, exactly one `[0, "mouse", x, y]`, and `308 <= x < 1058`, `180 <= y < 680` (`LIE_CURSOR_BOX`).

key_items.name: _lie_click_refusal
key_items.signature: def _lie_click_refusal(plan: dict, boxes, what: str, button: str) -> str | None
key_items.summary: The one allowed click shape shared by `lie_ok_refusal` (the pass dialog's OK, `LIE_OK_BOX`) and `lie_answer_refusal` (a Violetta button, `LIE_ANSWER_BOXES`).
key_items.details_md: No resize, recording, focus, lead or final wait; exactly three events: a move at 0 ms to a point inside one of `boxes`, then left button down and up; down within `LIE_CLICK_DOWN_MS` (1-1500 ms) and held `LIE_CLICK_HOLD_MS` (30-300 ms). control.client sends the button down at 1000 ms and up 80 ms later.

key_items.name: Alarm
key_items.summary: The Lie Detector seen: an Event that also remembers `at`, the time.monotonic() of its first `set`.
key_items.details_md: Set by the Watchdog, cleared by it only when an answered cycle is over (`_resume`). Every normal plan's key waits are on this event, so setting it ends them at once; `at` starts the retreat's 12 s window.

key_items.name: Watchdog._scores
key_items.summary: Chooses how much of the frame to search: only near each form's usual places on most looks, the whole frame when needed.
key_items.details_md: `spotter.near` on a 1366x768 frame with either capture anchor in place (`framecheck.anchors_off`: the minimap's title strip, the HUD's border; 0.04 ms). The whole frame (`spotter.scores`) on every `WHOLE_EVERY`-th look (8: a form shown anywhere else is seen within 2 s), throughout a cycle, on frames of any other size, and when neither anchor is in place (the game drawing its picture off its client moves every form off its places too). At 4 looks a second on saved hunt frames: 0.07-0.12 cores against 0.55-0.58 with the whole frame every look. Of 16,050 saved 1366x768 frames, the 3,809 that show a form all have an anchor in place.

key_items.name: Watchdog._grab
key_items.summary: Grabs the game's client area with mss: the frame, (frame, "covered"), or why there is none.
key_items.details_md: Asks Windows whether the window is minimized (a minimized client reports 432x54, not 0x0). `covered` when `window.shows` finds another window over the middle or near a corner: still checked for the Lie Detector (it can show round that window) but never saved, and it counts as gone when nothing is seen. A client of any size other than 1366x768 or 1920x1080 (full screen at 3840x2160, say) is resized to 1920x1080, the templates' size (`lie_detector.to_template`): before that, no saved Lie Detector screen was seen at such sizes (0.53-0.78 of the thresholds).

key_items.name: Watchdog._resume
key_items.summary: An answered Lie Detector's cycle over: deletes the alarm file and clears the alarm, so plans are taken again with no restart.
key_items.details_md: Only when the cycle saw no Truth Booth, the alarm file was written and is still there, and `auto_resume` is on (`AUTO_RESUME`, the user on 2026-10-29: "Stop requesting uac after a lie detector. Just detect that I manually solved it and carry on"). A file that can't be deleted keeps it locked. Seen again later, it's a new cycle and input stops at once.

key_items.name: _serve
key_items.summary: The plan loop: polls the inbox every 10 ms, claims, runs and answers plans until a stop condition.
key_items.details_md: Stops on `lab/STOP`, `watchdog.cleared`, 24 idle hours (idle time resets after each plan and while a Lie Detector recording or its post-test cycle runs), or the watchdog thread dying ("nothing would see one"). Takes no plan before the watchdog's first look. A spliced run answers under the last plan's id. On the way out it waits up to 30 s for the watchdog to finish its alarm, paging and recording (exiting at once had once killed it mid-write: no ALARM.json, an empty screenshot) and, with the alarm set, answers every waiting plan with the Lie Detector error.

key_items.name: allowed_keys
key_items.signature: def allowed_keys(keys: GameKeys | None = None, extra=ALL_KEYS) -> dict[str, Key]
key_items.summary: Her bound in-game actions plus every key config.toml can name (`ALL_KEYS`), by name.
key_items.details_md: Since 2026-10-23 the player may press any key config.toml can name and both mouse buttons (the in-game key bindings window, `\`, needs clicks to save a change); until then only her bound keys, `\` and Esc.

key_items.name: alarm_up
key_items.summary: Whether `lab/ALARM.json` exists; when that can't be told, it does (the lock stays).
key_items.details_md: Uses `os.stat`: missing -> False, any other OSError -> True. `Path.exists` answers False for any error on the Python used here (3.15), so an alarm file it couldn't look at had read as cleared.

modules.concurrency: One elevated process (started by `python -m gamelab player --elevate` through ShellExecute "runas": a UAC prompt). Main thread: the serve loop (10 ms polls, inside win32.precise_timers) and, during a plan that records, the mss capture. A `key-player` thread per plan (press_keys). The `lie-detector-watch` daemon thread (Watchdog, 4 looks a second). Per Lie Detector cycle, lie_recorder's writer and prune threads; per phone push, notify's threads.

tunables.name: IDLE_LIMIT_S
tunables.meaning: idle seconds before the player exits by itself (not while it records a Lie Detector)

tunables.name: MAX_EVENTS
tunables.meaning: events in one plan at most

tunables.name: MAX_PLAN_MS
tunables.meaning: a plan's events, end and capture all within 20 s

tunables.name: MAX_FRAMES
tunables.meaning: frames one plan may record

tunables.name: TAP_MAX_MS
tunables.meaning: with the alarm up: a pet-food tap is over and any plan starts within this

tunables.name: AUTO_RESUME
tunables.meaning: an answered Lie Detector (no Truth Booth) clears its own alarm and plans resume

tunables.name: LOG_MAX_BYTES
tunables.meaning: player.log rotated at start past this (about 30 hours of hunting)

tunables.name: READ_RETRY_S
tunables.meaning: a claimed plan refused by Windows (another program has it open) is read again for this long

tunables.name: WAIT_STEP_S
tunables.meaning: the key thread's sleep step between cancel/splice/alarm checks

tunables.name: FINAL_S
tunables.meaning: the last stretch before a key's time, waited precisely

tunables.name: Watchdog interval
tunables.meaning: seconds between the starts of two looks (4 a second)

tunables.name: SPLICE
tunables.meaning: written to lab/player.json: this player takes splices

decisions.what: Any key config.toml can name and both mouse buttons may be pressed; the pointer moves only inside the game
decisions.why: The key bindings window (\) needs a click on Confirm to save a change.

decisions.what: Idle limit raised from 3 hours to 24 hours
decisions.why: The user asked that it not be exited proactively: starting it again needs their UAC click, and it had stopped overnight.

decisions.what: At the Lie Detector the player stays up, locked, and records the whole cycle instead of shutting down at once
decisions.why: Nothing it saved showed the Lie Detector being answered.

decisions.what: Four plan kinds (pet food, retreat; later the Lie Detector cursor and OK click) still go with the alarm up
decisions.why: The user, after a Lie Detector failed while the alarm kept the pet from being fed: "just stop any in-progress hunt when this happens, don't block pet feeding", and "On a lie detector you should move to a safe place, within 10s".

decisions.what: The watchdog also recognizes the mini-game's notice and the image quiz's warning
decisions.why: Both come 10 s / 30 s before their test; the hunt had attacked through them.

decisions.what: Clients of other sizes are brought to 1920x1080 before the Lie Detector check
decisions.why: No saved Lie Detector screen was seen at other sizes (0.53-0.78 of the thresholds), and Alt+Enter puts the game full screen on purpose (control.window_size).

decisions.what: AUTO_RESUME: an answered Lie Detector clears its own alarm

modules.title: The Lie Detector alarm
modules.tagline: The alarm file, paging at the PC, and the rules for what may run while it's up
modules.summary: The shared vocabulary of the Lie Detector lock: the alarm file `lab/ALARM.json` (`raise_alarm`, `clear_alarm`, `alarm_info`), paging whoever is at the PC with beeps and a Windows toast (`page`), the four plan kinds that still run with the alarm up and their exact click boxes and limits, and `AlarmKeys`, which lets the elevated player follow her move and pet-food keys when they are rebound in the game. It imports nothing of gamelab but `paths` at load time, because the elevated player loads it.
modules.details_md:
### The alarm file
`raise_alarm(frame, reason, form, cause)` writes `{"reason", "time", "at", "form"?, "cause"?}` first (everything after it may fail), then saves the frame as `lab/lie_detector_<HHMMSS>.png` and writes the file again with `screenshot`. Paging runs in a `finally`, so an alarm that can't be written (disk full) is still paged before its error is raised; until that change nobody was told. `at` is `time.time()` at the sighting: her retreat counts its 10 s from it, and the player uses it when the alarm was raised by another program. While the file exists every gamelab command that sends keys refuses to run (control.client, exit code 3); `clear_alarm` (the `clear-alarm` command) deletes it. Raisers: the player's Watchdog, `watch --lie-detector`, and control.window_size when it sees the Lie Detector before an Alt+Enter.

### Paging
`page(title, text)`: three `MessageBeep`s 0.4 s apart (about 1.2 s), then a Windows toast (PowerShell, ToastText02) started hidden so the game keeps focus. The text depends on the form (`PAGED`): "MapleStory Lie Detector mini-game in 10 s", "MapleStory image quiz in 30 s", and so on; otherwise `PAGE`. The phone is control.notify's job.

### What still runs with the alarm up
`PLAN_KINDS`, checked in player.alarm_refusal:

| Kind | What | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| `pet_food` | one tap of her pet-food key | 3 a minute (`PET_FOOD_PER_MIN`) |
| `retreat` | her arrows, jump, up and down | until 12 s after the sighting (`RETREAT_WINDOW_S`); the hunt plans to be safe by 10 s (`RETREAT_S`) |
| `lie_cursor` | one move inside the board `LIE_CURSOR_BOX`, or one click on a Violetta button (`LIE_ANSWER_BOXES`) | click down 1-1500 ms in, held 30-300 ms |
| `lie_ok` | one click on the pass dialog's OK (`LIE_OK_BOX`) | same click timing |

The boxes are client pixels copied from perception (the board's `BOARD_AT_NATIVE`, Violetta's `BUTTON_AT`), because the elevated player must not import those modules.

### Her keys followed
config.toml is read once at the player's start, but the running commands follow her keys when they move in the game (control.keymap publishes `lab/alarm_keys.json`). `AlarmKeys.current()` re-reads the file whenever its size or mtime changes and accepts it only if `alarm_keys_problem` finds nothing wrong: only `ALARM_FIELDS`; each a key config.toml can name; none of `ALARM_UNSAFE` (Esc, `\`, Enter, Tab, Backspace, the digits: keys that could answer the Lie Detector or open game windows); her five moves on five keys; pet food not on a move key; arrows and jump bound. A field the file puts on a key config.toml uses for another of her actions goes on no key with the alarm up (`_clashes`). A bad file is left out (config.toml's keys used) and said once per change.

### Saving the recent recording
`keep_recent` / `keep_recent_after` ask the rolling recorder (control.rolling.ask) to save its last N seconds, never raising; used by behavior (the out-of-darts stop, the hunter's no-hit saves, a retreat's stop). rolling is imported only when asked, since the player loads this module.

modules.title: Notifications: phone and text
modules.tagline: Bark critical alerts to the iPhone and email-to-SMS texts, never in the player's way
modules.summary: Pages the user's phone without ever blocking the player: `Pusher` (owned by the player's Watchdog) sends a critical Bark alert and an email-to-SMS text at a Lie Detector's first sight, again once if it turns into the Truth Booth, and an ordinary push when it's gone. `phone` sends the hunt's own pushes, critical or regular (her potions and death from behavior.vitals, the guard, a park that failed or was put off); `BackpackPush` a regular one when her backpack is full. Config lives in git-ignored `lab/bark.json` and `lab/smtp.json`, read again at every push.
modules.details_md:
The PC's own beeps and toast (control.alarm.page) stay; this module adds the phone, because a push sent by whoever drove gamelab came late (the user, 2026-10-29: "I need a better notification method, I didn't catch the notification in time to solve this").

### Bark (iPhone)
`bark_url` builds Bark's GET form, `{server}/{key}/{title}/{body}?level=...&group=gamelab`, with `volume=10` at level `critical` and `sound=alarm` unless the caller passes none (the regular pushes of `phone` and `BackpackPush` use the phone's own sound; Pusher's "gone" push keeps `alarm`) (Bark's critical alerts are documented to ignore silent and Do Not Disturb modes; ntfy's iOS app, used before, couldn't). `call=1` (its sound repeated for 30 s) only if the file says `"ring": true`. A Bark answer must have code 200 (or none). Timeout 10 s.

### Text (SMS by email)
`send_mail` sends through the user's own SMTP account with STARTTLS (port 587 by default) to the addresses in `lab/smtp.json` (a carrier's email-to-text gateway), timeout 20 s, kept short (gateways keep about 160 characters). `setup_mail` (`notify --setup-sms`) makes the file with the login left empty for the user to fill in themselves.

### The Lie Detector's pushes: `Pusher`
| When | Title | Level | Text too |
|---|---|---|---|
| a cycle's first sight | "Lie Detector up" (or "Lie Detector missed" if first seen as the Truth Booth, noting an unknown cause) | critical | yes |
| the Truth Booth later in the cycle, once | "Lie Detector missed" | critical | yes |
| the cycle's end | "Lie Detector gone" | active | no |

There is no repeated "still up" reminder (removed on 2026-11-04). The text holds only the form, the time and how long it has been up: never a screenshot, her name or the map.

### Never in the way
Each push and each mail runs on its own daemon thread with a timeout, and never raises: failures are logged with the Bark key replaced by `<key>`. No config file, nothing sent; each file is read at each push, so one set up while a player runs is used without a restart. Under `GAMELAB_NO_PUSH` (set by the tests' conftest) the lab's files are never read: on 2026-10-29 a test run in the main checkout had texted the user a Lie Detector from a test's fake screen.

modules.title: The Lie Detector cycle recorder
modules.tagline: An index of every watchdog look from a Lie Detector's first sight to its end
modules.summary: For each Lie Detector cycle the player's watchdog makes a `Recording`: a folder `lab/lie_detector/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>/` with `index.jsonl` (a line a look: time, the spotter's score per form, or why there was no frame) and, at the end, `summary.json` (forms seen and when, outcome, cause, the Truth Booth stay's end). Writing happens on its own thread behind a queue, so a slow disk never holds up the watchdog. Since 2026-11-01 it keeps no pictures: the cycle's video is the rolling recorder's clip.
modules.details_md:
### What a look adds
`add(t, frame, scores, why)` is called every look (4 a second). A frame contributes only its size and a frame number `i`; without one, `game` says why ("no window", "minimized", or "covered" with the scores of what was on top). Each form scoring at least 1 updates `forms[name]` (first, last, frames); any form but the Truth Booth sets `test_last`. Lines go into a queue of `QUEUE_ITEMS` (16, about 4 s of looks); the `lie-detector-recording` thread appends each to `index.jsonl`, opening and closing the file every time so its last write shows. When the disk falls behind a line is dropped and the next line's `dropped_before` says how many.

### How it ends
`finish(end)` returns at once; the writer drains the queue and writes `summary.json`. It reads the `ended` flag *before* the queue, so a look added just before the end is never lost. End reasons: `gone` (no Lie Detector for `END_S`, 10 s), `test over` (the test, every form but the Truth Booth, unseen for `TEST_TAIL_S`, 5 s), `cap` (`CAP_S`, 10 minutes after the first sight: the longest cycle seen, a test left unanswered then the Truth Booth, is about 8 minutes), `stopped` (the player stopped). Outcome: "sent to the Truth Booth" if it showed, "answered" if the Lie Detector went away without it, else "unknown: still up when the recording ended".

A recording that ended at its test's end while the cycle goes on (the Truth Booth) has a `cycle.live` file the watchdog touches every look (`cycle_going`) and removes at the cycle's end (`cycle_over`, which also adds a late Truth Booth to the summary). `going()` tells `clear-alarm` whether a cycle is still in progress (an index or live file written within `LIVE_S`, 5 s): `clear-alarm` refuses until then.

### The Truth Booth
A failed test sends her to the Truth Booth. `booth_until` (when its on-screen clock says the stay ends, read by the watchdog) goes into the summary; `last_booth_until` reads it back when a player starts, so a player started again inside the booth doesn't take it for a new sighting of unknown cause. `UNKNOWN_CAUSE` marks a Truth Booth first seen with no test before it ("we missed some kind of check"); a stay whose clock was never read ends `BOOTH_UNREAD_S` (10 minutes) after its first sight.

### Disk
When a recording starts, `prune` (on its own thread) deletes the oldest recordings until the rest take at most `KEEP_BYTES` (10 GB), never the one being written. Most of the bytes are the rolling recorder's `before/` (about 650 MB each), so about 15 cycles fit. It records nothing of the mouse or keyboard and never touches the game; it imports nothing of gamelab but paths, since the elevated player loads it.

modules.title: Live mini-game target tracking
modules.tagline: Follows the mouse mini-game's target on the service's frames and moves the cursor through the player
modules.summary: Runs inside the perception service. While the alarm file is up, `LieTracking` keeps the newest frame, looks for the mouse mini-game's board, and during a round sends board crops to a tracker child process (perception.lie_target.TargetTracker). Each answer (the target's centre in board, client and desktop px) goes to a per-round file and to telemetry, and a cursor thread hands the newest position to the elevated player as a `lie_cursor` move.
modules.details_md:
### Rounds
`saw` (on the frame loop) keeps only the newest frame, and only while the alarm is up or a round is on; the `lie-target` thread's `step` takes it. The alarm file is looked at once every 0.5 s at most (`ALARM_POLL_S`); one that can't be looked at counts as up. Before a round the board is looked for every 0.25 s (`BOARD_CHECK_S`) with the spotter's `over_play` ("mini-game"); a round begins at its first sight and ends when the board has been unseen 3 s (`BOARD_GONE_S`), the alarm goes, or after 60 s (`ROUND_MAX_S`; the longest seen was 10.4 s from START). In a round the board is checked once a second (`BOARD_ROUND_S`, 4 ms a look); frames after a look without it aren't sent and the cursor stops, going on if the board shows again within 3 s. Only 1366x768 frames are used: the board's place, `BOARD_AT_NATIVE` (308, 180, 750x500), is known at that size.

### The tracker process
`Child` starts `python -m gamelab.control.lie_tracking <folder> <fps>` at below-normal priority with OpenCV on 6 threads (`CHILD_THREADS`) when the alarm goes up, and it is stopped 60 s after the alarm has gone (`CHILD_IDLE_S`). Messages are pickled down its stdin (`begin`, `frame` with the 750x500 RGB board crop and the client's screen corner, `end`, `quit`); replies come up its stdout (`ready` with the answer line or None, `ended`, `error`). One frame is in flight at a time: a new frame goes only when the child said `ready`; frames in between are skipped and counted. Why a process: in the service, whose OpenCV runs on one thread, a frame took 78 ms against 52-64 on 6-12 threads, over the 66 ms of 15 frames a second, and it would share the frame loop's Python lock.

### Answers
`serve` (in the child) steps the TargetTracker on each crop and writes `lab/lie_target/<round>.jsonl`: a header line, a template line whenever the tracker takes a new white-star template (its outline and normals, so an answer can be redrawn without its frame), an answer line per frame (`t`, `at`, `seq`, `run`, `board`, `client` = board + (308, 180), `desktop` = client + the window's corner, `angle`, `score`, `white`, `template`, `ms`), and an end line (frames, answers, skipped, frames without the board, median and worst ms). Answers also go to the service's telemetry (`lie_target`, `lie_target_round`, `lie_target_cursor`).

### The cursor
`_queue_cursor` keeps only the newest target; the `lie-target-cursor` thread calls `client.move_lie_cursor` with client coordinates: one `lie_cursor` plan `[0, "mouse", x, y]`, which the player checks against `LIE_CURSOR_BOX` and plays as a generated trail (`window.move_cursor`), the trail coming back in the plan's result. The plan is cancelled when the round ends or the board disappears (`_cursor_wait`). A mover failure turns only the cursor off (`cursor_why_off`); tracking and its records go on. The ordinary service can't move the pointer itself: the administrator game blocks its input. Only the cursor moves inside the board: never a button or a key.

modules.title: Live Violetta solver
modules.tagline: Follows the Violetta shuffle game, clicks the answer, and clicks the pass dialog's OK
modules.summary: Also in the perception service. When the alarm goes up it loads the Violetta YOLO model (perception.violetta) on a background thread; from the countdown window's first sight it detects the Violettas on every frame, solves each round when the four answer buttons light up, and clicks the made-up Violetta's button through the player (`client.click_lie_answer`, a `lie_cursor` click). After a pass it clicks the "You have successfully passed" dialog's OK (`client.click_lie_ok`). `Together` bundles it with LieTracking as the service's one Lie Detector watcher.
modules.details_md:
The Violetta game ("Keep your eyes on the Violetta who's wearing make-up") is the countdown form's test: four Violettas shuffle and the player must click the button under the made-up one.

### Following a game
- `saw` queues the frame loop's frames (at most `QUEUE` = 45, about 3 s; past it the oldest is dropped and counted) while the alarm is up, a game is on, or for `AFTER_S` (90 s) after the alarm went: the pass dialog shows after the game.
- The model is loaded on a `violetta-load` thread as the alarm goes up, before the game's window shows (its box comes 10 s and its window 15 s more before the shuffles). A load failure turns the watcher off (`why_off`); the service goes on.
- A game begins at the first look (every 0.25 s, `WINDOW_CHECK_S`) where the spotter's `over_play` says "countdown"; during it the window is checked once a second; it ends when unseen 3 s (`WINDOW_GONE_S`) or after 150 s (`GAME_MAX_S`; 4 rounds take about 60 s). Only 1366x768 frames are used.
- Every frame: the detector's boxes and the frame's time are kept. On the frame where the buttons light up (`violetta.buttons_lit`), `_round` runs: on the first window the four slots (`slots_of`) and the made-up one's start slot (`start_slot`) are measured on the frames before it; each round's permutation comes from `solve_round` on the frames since the last window, knowing the answer window's time (its `window` argument), and the slot is chained `where = perm[where]`. The shuffle is fitted to the client's own rules (one hop or two, the motion 3.8-5.0 s, per the README).
- The answer is logged and recorded (`violetta` telemetry: `begin`, `round`, `answer`, `end`, `ok`), with no phone push per round, and clicked on a `violetta-answer` thread: `BUTTON_AT[slot - 1]` through `client.click_lie_answer`, whose `active` turns false once the buttons go dark or the game ends, so the plan is withdrawn or cancelled.

### The pass dialog
Every 0.5 s (`OK_CHECK_S`) `violetta.OkDialog` looks for it; seen on 2 looks in a row (`OK_SEEN`) its OK is clicked through `client.click_lie_ok` (one click inside `LIE_OK_BOX`, the game the window under the pointer), at most 3 times (`OK_TRIES`) a minute and 3 s apart (`OK_RETRY_S`) while it stays.

modules.title: The rolling recording
modules.tagline: The game's last 5 minutes kept losslessly in memory, saved on alarms or on demand
modules.summary: A `Recorder` keeps a `Ring` of moments (a compressed frame, or a gap and why) covering the last 300 s, at most 4 GB. It is fed by its own mss grabs 10 times a second (`gamelab recorder`) or, in the perception service, by the service's own frames 15 times a second (control.recording). On a Lie Detector alarm it saves the 5 minutes before into the player's cycle folder (`before/`) and writes a lossless clip of the cycle; `save-recent` asks it for the last N seconds through a file inbox.
modules.details_md:
### Moments and the ring
Each `Item` is one moment: `t` (wall clock) and either `data` (the pixels, zstd level 1 through Python 3.14's `compression.zstd`, zlib on older Pythons) or a gap with `why` ("no window", "minimized", "no client area", "off the screen", "covered", "moved", "capture failed", "not encoded"). Frames it grabs itself are packed whole (`pack`: BGRA to BGR into a per-thread buffer, then compressed; about 757 KB and 9.5 ms a 1366x768 frame). The perception service's frames are kept as their difference from the frame before (`pack_diff`: uint8 subtraction that wraps round; 332 KB against 482 whole), with a whole frame (`key=True`) at least every second: a *chain*. `decode` adds the differences back, giving exactly the frames shown. The `Ring` drops whole chains from the front once they are older than `SECONDS` (300), or past `MAX_BYTES` (4 GB, counted as `trimmed`) or `MAX_ITEMS` (twice the moments of 5 minutes: 6,000 at 10 a second, 9,000 in the service at 15).

Lossless since 2026-10-25 (the user asked): as JPEG with the usual half-resolution colour, the countdown's thin yellow title lost its colour and the spotter scored it 0.36-0.41 of its threshold.

### What counts as a frame
`GameWindow.check`: the window exists, isn't minimized, has a client area wholly on the monitors (`window.on_screen`); then the windows above it (`window.overs`). Wholly covered is a gap; partly covered keeps the frame and notes the covered boxes and share (`Item.over`, `Item.covered`; since 2026-11-01, when seven alarms' clips of 2026-10-29 had kept no frame at all). `tick` checks before and after the grab; a window that moved in between is a gap.

### Saving
`poll` runs between ticks: inbox requests (every tick), a new alarm (every 0.5 s, keyed by the alarm's `time`), clips that are due, the status file every 5 s, a log line every 10 minutes. Saves go on a queue to one `rolling-saves` thread at below-normal thread priority (`WRITER_PRIORITY` -1; the service's recording passes -2) and are written by `write_part`: frames as JPEG (quality 75, full-resolution colour) or PNG (level 1, no row filters), on 4 encoder threads, a chain at a time, plus `index.jsonl` and `summary.json`.

On an alarm `check_alarm` makes a `Clip` that holds the ring's snapshot (for `before/`) and every new moment (so the ring's cap can't lose them). Once the player's recording of the cycle has a summary, `cycle_end` ends the clip 5 s after the test's last sight (`CLIP_TAIL_S`), and at most 180 s after the alarm (`CLIP_MAX_S`). Then `_save_clip` writes PNG frames from 2 s (`CLIP_BEFORE_S`) before the first frame where the spotter sees the Lie Detector (looked for from 3 s before the alarm) to `lab/alarm_clips/<stamp>-lie-detector[-form]/`, and `_save_before` writes the 5 minutes before plus the alarm's first 5 s (JPEG) into the cycle folder's `before/` (found by its name, 2 s before to 20 s after the alarm; none: `lab/recent`). Writing waits for the cycle's end so heavy encoding doesn't run while the Lie Detector is up. A Truth Booth of unknown cause has its 5 minutes written at once, PNG, to `lab/booth_unknown/`. Each folder is pruned to its budget: recent 20 GB, clips 30 GB, unknown-cause 20 GB, Lie Detector recordings 10 GB.

### One recorder, and asking it
`only_one` holds the named mutex `Local\gamelab-rolling-recorder`. `ask` is the command line's side of `save-recent`: it writes a request into `lab/recorder/inbox/`, withdraws it if not taken (renamed `.taken`) within 3 s, and waits up to 180 s for the answer in `lab/recorder/outbox/`. `status_lines` prints `recorder --status`.

modules.title: The perception service's recording
modules.tagline: Feeds the rolling recorder from the perception service's own 15 fps frames
modules.summary: Since 2026-10-26 the rolling recording lives inside the perception service (`gamelab perceive`). `Recording.saw` takes the frame loop's frames without ever waiting, a token bucket keeps 15 a second, an encoder thread stores each as a difference from the one before, and a ticks thread runs the rolling Recorder's polling and takes its own mss grabs when the frame loop is silent or too slow. Saves are written by a separate partwriter process.
modules.details_md:
### Taking frames
`saw(st, frame, run)` is called by the service for every state it emits. It skips frames that don't show the game wholly (`frame.visible`), whose capture is offset from the window (`GAP_KINDS`), or whose cover check wasn't made (`frame.over is None`). A token bucket (`FPS` = 15 tokens a second, `BURST` = 2) picks frames by their own times: a loop slower than 15 a second has all its frames kept, and after a stall at most one extra. On the replays' real frame times a loop at 12-14 a second kept 11.6-13.2, at 25-30 a second 15.0. The picture is passed by reference (perception.frames never overwrites a picture while it's held; never a shared-memory slot: encoding from one crashed the service when a new run unmapped it) onto a queue of `QUEUE` = 8; past it the frame is dropped and counted. Another window over all of the game (or over it where the boxes aren't known) makes a `covered` gap; over part of it, the frame is kept with its boxes.

### Encoding
The `perceive-recording-encoder` thread's `encode` stores a difference (`rolling.pack_diff`) unless a whole frame is due (`KEY_EVERY_S` = 1 s), the size changed, or another moment came in between (then `Recorder.add(after=...)` refuses and a whole frame is stored). Frames older than the ring's newest moment are dropped as `late`. Measured: 180-375 KB and 4-7 ms of CPU a frame, so 5 minutes at 15 a second take 0.5-1.6 GB. Keeping camera-pan frames whole saved only 3-5% for 65% more CPU, so it isn't done.

### Its own moments
The `perceive-recording` ticks thread runs 15 times a second. When the frame loop has handed nothing over for `OWN_AFTER_S` (0.25 s: the game not on screen, another client size, a stalled capture) it calls `rolling.Recorder.tick` itself. When the loop gives fewer than `FLOOR_FPS` (10) frames in the last second it takes the *floor*: its own grabs, until the loop gives `FLOOR_BACK_FPS` (12) a second over `FLOOR_BACK_S` (2 s); the loop's frames meanwhile are only counted. Then it polls (inbox, alarm, clips, status).

### One recorder
`take` grabs the rolling mutex first. While `gamelab recorder` holds it, the service writes `lab/recorder/waiting.json` and tries again every 10 s; the babysitter stops the old recorder when it sees this and it has nothing left to write.

### Saves
The Recorder is made with `apart=True`: parts are written by a partwriter child process with 4 writer threads (`WRITERS`; 2 while a hunting command is attached), the saver thread at `WRITER_PRIORITY` (-2, the lowest). Written in the service, a save shared Python's lock with the frame loop whatever the priority. It can't outlive the service: a service that ends loses the 5 minutes it held.

modules.tagline: A child process that encodes and writes one saved part of the rolling recording
modules.summary: `python -m gamelab.control.partwriter` reads a pickled header and N rolling `Item`s from stdin, writes the part with `rolling.write_part` at the lowest thread priority, and prints one JSON line (`{"summary": ...}` or `{"error": ...}`). It exists so the perception service's saves don't share Python's lock with its frame loop.
modules.details_md:
Started by `rolling.write_part_apart` with no window and a below-normal priority class (Idle if its parent is Idle). The header carries `folder`, `info`, `fps`, `png`, `encoders` and `n`; then each moment is pickled as the Item's fields in order (`t, data, why, size, key, rgb, seq, run, covered, over`), the compressed frame bytes passed through as they are (pickle protocol 5 writes a big buffer straight out).

It sets OpenCV to one thread (its writers are the threads) and every thread, the writers too, to `LOWEST` (-2). Writers at normal priority had still taken CPUs from the frame loop on the replays (its rate 11.4 to 8.0 frames a second during a 120 s save, the machine 54% busy).

On any failure it prints `{"error": ...}` and exits 1; the parent then writes the part itself, after moving a half-written folder aside. The parent also kills it past `APART_TIMEOUT_S` (600 s; 300 s of frames took 24-31 s written in the service).

modules.title: Window sizing (Alt+Enter twice)
modules.tagline: Sets the game's client back to 1366x768 with Alt+Enter twice, guarded against the Lie Detector
modules.summary: The eyes only work on a 1366x768 client drawn where its window is. When the client is another size or the game draws its picture off the client (framecheck's fault kinds `size` and `drawn`), `SizeFix` makes a `refit` try: Alt+Enter through the key player to go full screen, then Alt+Enter again to come back windowed at the game's own size, the way the user fixes it by hand. Every press is guarded: no alarm, no Lie Detector on the picture, no plan running, one process at a time, the game in front.
modules.details_md:
### One try: `refit`
- Not tried (`held`) with the game minimized, the alarm up, `client.busy()` (a plan waiting for the player or being played), or another process holding the named mutex `Local\gamelab-window-fix`.
- From windowed: one Alt+Enter (`ALT_ENTER`: Alt down, Enter down at 50 ms, Enter up at 90 ms, Alt up at 140 ms; each Alt+Enter is a plan of its own through `client.submit`), then `_settle` waits for the client area to change within 8 s (`CHANGE_S`) and stay the same 1.5 s (`SETTLE_S`), polled every 0.1 s, 20 s at most. If it is now full screen, it waits until 8 s (`FULL_HOLD_S`) after the player answered that press, then sends Alt+Enter back, pressing again up to 3 times (`BACK_PRESSES`) while a press changes nothing.
- No second press after a first that set the size right or didn't reach full screen: a second would leave the game full screen.
- Before *every* press (`_press`): the game not minimized, the alarm not up, any busy plan waited for (10 s, on the way back), the game brought to the front (3 s), and the Lie Detector looked for on the perception service's picture of the client at whatever size (`spot`, usually `lie_detector_sighting`: the picture brought to 1920x1080, the spotter's templates' size). Seen: `_alarm` raises the alarm as the player's watchdog would (it may not see it at this size). No picture: no Alt+Enter; after a first press the look is asked again every 0.5 s for 8 s (`LOOK_FOR_S`), then the try stops, the game left full screen.
- The outcome is a `Refit` and a log line (also a telemetry `event` of kind `window`).

### When to try: `SizeFix`
A hunting command's Senses hand it every look's `Problem` that left nothing to act on. Only `FIX_KINDS` faults count. It tries once the same fault, the window where it was, has stood 5 s (`STEADY_S`: never in the middle of the user's own drag), once more 30 s later (`AGAIN_S`), and after `TRIES` (2) gives up and waits for the user, until a look passes. `HOURLY` (4) tries an hour at most across all processes (`lab/window_tries.json`). Before a try it checks the game is in play: the HUD's buttons match at least 0.7 (`HUD_SEEN`), so Enter never goes into a login or character-select field. A try is counted as its first Alt+Enter goes to the player (`on_try`), so one killed in the hold still counts; tries that sent nothing are counted apart (`UNPRESSED`, 4). `pending()` lets a command's looks wait for the first try (up to `STEADY_S` + `HOLD_S` = 15 s) before giving up.

Alt is her jump key too: she jumps where she stands at each Alt+Enter. Only `FULL_HOLD_S` is measured; the other waits are guesses that `window --recover`'s settle times are meant to check.

flows.title: From a Lie Detector sighting to its end
flows.summary: How one sighting stops the keys, raises the alarm, pages, records, lets the mini-game helpers act through the player, and finally unlocks (or doesn't).
flows.trigger: A Watchdog look scores some Lie Detector form at or above its threshold with no cycle in progress

steps.text: The look (one of 4 a second) sees a form: `alarm.set()` comes first, before any file or sound.
The key thread's `wait` was sleeping on that event: it returns at once, `press_keys` stops, the `finally` lets go of every held key and the plan is answered with the Lie Detector error.
The watchdog's `_raise` writes lab/ALARM.json (time, `at`, form, cause), saves the screenshot and pages: 3 beeps and a Windows toast.
A recording folder lab/lie_detector/<stamp>/ starts with this first look; every later look adds a line.
A critical Bark alert and a text go out on threads of their own.
Within 0.5 s the rolling recorder sees a new alarm time, snapshots its 5-minute ring and starts holding a clip.

Seeing the alarm file, the service starts the target tracker child and, on the mouse mini-game's board, sends the cursor's moves to the player as `lie_cursor` plans; the Violetta watcher (violetta_live) likewise loads its model and clicks answers.
Meanwhile every plan is refused but the four kinds: the hunt's retreat (12 s), pet-food taps, the cursor moves and the two click forms.
The recording ends 5 s after the test's last sight (or when nothing has been seen 10 s); its thread writes summary.json.

With the summary there, the clip ends 5 s after `test_last`; the clip (PNG) and before/ (JPEG) are then written, by a partwriter process in the perception service (the standalone `gamelab recorder` writes them itself).

Gone 10 s with no Truth Booth: the alarm file is deleted and the alarm cleared, plans resume with no restart. A Truth Booth cycle stays locked until `clear-alarm`; then the player stops and needs a UAC click.

flows.title: How a plan becomes key presses
flows.summary: The file handshake between an unelevated command and the elevated player, and how the keys are timed.
flows.trigger: A command calls control.client.send or submit, which writes lab/inbox/<id>.json

steps.text: Polling every 10 ms, the player takes the first plan by name and claims it by renaming it `<id>.running`; the client can now only cancel it.
Reads the JSON, retrying every 5 ms for up to 0.5 s while Windows refuses the file; the id comes from the sanitized file name.
Checks events, times, sizes and capture; then the cursor/click shapes and, with the alarm up, `alarm_refusal`.
Resizes the client or brings the game to the front if asked, refuses if the game isn't in front, and starts the `key-player` thread; the main thread records frames if asked.

For each event the key thread's `wait` sleeps on the halt event in 15 ms steps (`WAIT_STEP_S`), checking `.cancel`, a retreat's cutoff and a waiting splice between, then reaches the key's time with `_sleep_until` (the last 20 ms, spinning only the final 4 ms); it checks the foreground again and presses (`_press`, SendInput) or moves the pointer along a generated trail.

`Player.run`'s `finally` lets go of every held key; `_serve` then has `_answer` write the result to lab/outbox/<id>.tmp and rename it to <id>.json (frames, if recorded, to <id>.npz); control.client.wait picks it up.

flows.title: The mouse mini-game's cursor, from frame to pointer
flows.summary: How the perception service follows the fading figure and moves the real pointer through the elevated player.
flows.trigger: The alarm file is up and the mouse mini-game's board shows

steps.text: The service's frame loop hands over each frame; only the newest is kept.
The board is seen (`over_play` says 'mini-game'): a round begins, and each 750x500 board crop is sent to the tracker child when it is ready.
The child steps perception.lie_target.TargetTracker, writes the answer line to lab/lie_target/<round>.jsonl and replies with it.
The answer goes to telemetry and, if the board is still showing, becomes the cursor thread's newest target.
The cursor thread calls control.client.move_lie_cursor with client px: a `lie_cursor` plan of one move at 0 ms, cancelled if the round ends first.
The player accepts only one move at 0 ms inside the board's box, no focus, no wait.
window.move_cursor plays a generated trail to the point; the trail comes back in the result and into the `move finished` telemetry record.

flows.title: Setting a wrong-sized client right
flows.summary: From a failed look to Alt+Enter twice through the player, and the guards on every press.
flows.trigger: A hunting command's look has nothing to act on because of a framecheck fault of kind `size` or `drawn`

steps.text: The same fault has stood 5 s, tries are left (2 each time, 4 an hour across processes), no alarm, and the HUD shows the game in play: try.
Held off if minimized, the alarm is up, a plan is busy, or another process holds the window-fix mutex; else it takes the mutex.
Brings the game forward and looks for the Lie Detector on the service's picture of the client; seen, it raises the alarm instead of pressing.
The Alt+Enter plan (Alt down, Enter at 50-90 ms, Alt up at 140 ms) is played with the game in front.
Waits for the client to change within 8 s and stay 1.5 s.
Full screen now: waits until 8 s after the first press, then Alt+Enter back (up to 3 presses if one changes nothing); refit reads the size and says whether it's 1366x768 windowed.

not_done: window_size has not run in game apart from the user's own Alt+Enters of 2026-10-25 23:41; all its waits but FULL_HOLD_S are guesses (README: Capture checks).
Whether the player's watchdog grab sees a full-screen game at all isn't known, and the window-size in-play check has met no login, character-select or cash-shop screen (README).

lie_recorder.END_S (10 s) ends a cycle after 10 s with no form the spotter knows; its comment's worry (the mini-game's count and figure tracking unseen) predates the board's own form, and how long an unseen stretch can last live isn't measured. An early end clears an answered-looking cycle's alarm by itself (AUTO_RESUME).
The rolling recording kept by the perception service can't outlive it: a service that ends loses the 5 minutes it held (recording.py).
Lossless packing in the standalone recorder (about 0.17 of a core estimated) is not measured in the live loop yet (README: The rolling recording).
lie_tracking and violetta_live use only frames of the game's own 1366x768 size; at any other client size they follow nothing.
partwriter.py has only two symbols (main, LOWEST); its behaviour lives in rolling.write_part and write_part_apart.

Some docstrings and README lines still give older numbers: player.py's top and the README say the player stops after "a minute" off the screen (END_S is 10 s), rolling.py's top says the service records "every other frame of its 30 a second" (15, every frame, since 2026-10-30), and paths.ALARM_CLIPS says a clip runs "10 s before it to 60 s after" (2 s before the first frame showing it to 5 s after the test). The values here are the code's constants.
